text: The Hubble tension is the statistically significant (> 5σ) discrepancy between the value of the present‑day Hubble constant, \(H_0\), inferred from early‑universe measurements (primarily the cosmic microwave background, CMB, within the ΛCDM framework) and the value obtained from late‑time, local distance‑ladder determinations (e.g., Cepheid‑calibrated Type Ia supernovae). The CMB‑inferred value is about \(67.3\text{–}67.4\;\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}\,Mpc^{-1}}\) while local measurements give \(73\text{–}73.2\;\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}\,Mpc^{-1}}\) [2][4]. This tension is often called the “Hubble tension” and reflects a fundamental disagreement between two independent inference chains anchored at very different epochs of the Universe.
